title: Infinite sums and products: König’s theorem and restrictions on powers

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 45–47 (§10, Theorem 10.12 and Corollary 10.13; §11, Definition 11.1 and Theorem 11.6)

summary: König’s inequality links indexed sums and products and limits the possible sizes of power sets.
abstract: Combining an indexed family of sets can mean keeping one tagged copy of every point or choosing one point from every set. These constructions give infinite sums and products of sizes. Assuming the axiom of choice, König’s theorem says that making each size strictly larger before taking the product produces a size greater than the original sum. This comparison shows that raising an infinite size to its cofinality, the number of stages needed to approach it, makes it larger. As a consequence, no countable collection of smaller sizes can approach the size of the real numbers.
